newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen says Krupp to bear steel merger costs.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen says Krupp to bear steel merger costs.

text.p: Germany's Thyssen AG said on Thursday that the Krupp group would bear the full restructuring costs arising from the merger of the two companies' carbon steel operations.
Krupp will take A one-off charge of between 800 million and 1.3 billion marks to cover depreciation on assets and the costs of worker redundancies during a four-year restructuring period.

Thyssen chairman Dieter Vogel, speaking after his company's supervisory board approved a steel merger agreement reached on Wednesday with Fried. Krupp AG said Thyssen would receive up-front profits during the steel restructuring.

This was to balance out the difference in profitability at the two groups' steel operations, he said. Thyssen Stahl AG earns around 300 million marks a year more than the smaller Krupp Hoesch Stahl AG.
He added: "Krupp will receive a bank credit for the exact sum that will be defined in the next weeks. The restructuring costs will later be offset by synergy effects."
Pension liabilities for workers will not be taken over by the new company, Vogel said.

Separately, Thyssen said that Ulrich Cartellieri, board member of Deutsche Bank AG, would resign from the Thuyssen supervisory board effective May 20 -- when he is also due to step down from the Deutsche board.

Cartellieri had come under criticism for not informing Thyssen over a hostile takeover bid initially launched by Krupp backed by a three-bank group which included Deutsche which was later abandoned in favour of the steel merger.
